mechanism_narrative: The current level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is a negative predictor of S&P 500 forward returns. A higher FEDFUNDS rate increases the risk-free rate and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This signal is always active as FEDFUNDS is continuously available.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 300.0, it signals persistent inflation that triggers a monetary policy response, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The threshold is set at 300.0 based on historical data where CPI above this level has correlated with negative equity returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 300.0.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) drives S&P 500 returns. When FEDFUNDS is rising and CPIAUCSL is above 300.0, it indicates an aggressive monetary tightening cycle in response to high inflation, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increase > 0.2% in last month and CPIAUCSL > 300.0
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant: the negative return prediction holds in less than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises by >0.2% and CPIAUCSL > 300.0.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) and strong labor market growth (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% in the last month), the S&P 500 is expected to produce positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This regime indicates sustained economic growth without immediate inflationary pressure.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% in last month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1400.0 (thousands of units), it signals a weakening housing market and broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1400.0.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a broad economic slowdown. When HOUST falls below 1400.0 and INDPRO falls below 100.0, it signals a contraction in both the housing sector and manufacturing, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant: the negative return prediction holds in less than 40% of instances where HOUST < 1400.0 and INDPRO < 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100.0 (base 2017), it signals a manufacturing contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle regime (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL > 300.0), the S&P 500 is expected to produce negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days. This regime indicates aggressive policy response to high inflation, compressing equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL > 300.0.
